report_name: Vanderbilt University Hit by BYOD Ransomware; Attackers Claim Massive Data Theft

threat_actors.name: BYOD
threat_actors.description: An emerging ransomware group that first appeared in September 2026. It targets higher education and healthcare sectors and claimed responsibility for the ransomware attack against Vanderbilt University in November 2026.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through double-extortion tactics, involving data encryption and the exfiltration and threatened release of sensitive data.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The BYOD group claimed to have exfiltrated large volumes of sensitive data, including over one million Social Security numbers, student records, and research data, before deploying the ransomware. This is a standard double-extortion tactic.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The BYOD ransomware encrypted files on Vanderbilt University's systems, rendering them inaccessible. The attack also involved displaying ransom notes and playing an audio message to announce the compromise.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely deleted volume shadow copies using tools like vssadmin.exe to prevent easy recovery of encrypted files from local backups.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely used compromised credentials for initial access and privilege escalation, as evidenced by their claim of taking over a domain controller.

attack_patterns.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
attack_patterns.description: The attackers may have used wevtutil.exe to clear Windows Event Logs to cover their tracks and impede forensic investigation, a common defense evasion technique.

malware.name: BYOD Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the BYOD group to encrypt systems at Vanderbilt University. Its execution was accompanied by ransom notes and an audio message.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Used by the attackers to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery.

tools.name: wevtutil
tools.description: Likely used by attackers to clear Windows Event Logs to hide their activity.

identities.name: Vanderbilt University
identities.description: A major private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, targeted by the BYOD ransomware group in a significant cyberattack starting November 9, 2026.

infrastructure.name: BYOD Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web data leak site where the BYOD ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack on Vanderbilt University and threatened to publish exfiltrated data.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b8b3c1a-4d5e-4f6a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware TTP to inhibit system recovery.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-11
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/vanderbilt-university-hit-in-byod-ransomware-attack-data-theft-claimed/
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'delete shadows'
  condition: selection
